# Benchmarks

## Metrics
- AUROC
- AUPRC
- Precision, Recall
- FPR, FNR (focus on low FPR)
- Calibration Error (ECE)
- Inference latency

## Expected Baselines (to be measured, not fabricated)
- Statistical detectors alone: AUROC ~0.70-0.80 on in-domain
- + Fine-tuned XLM-R: AUROC ~0.85-0.92 on in-domain, ~0.75-0.85 generator-held-out
- Low FPR target: FPR <5% at 80% recall for English, <10% for Hinglish

## Reporting
- Always report per language, per generator, per domain
- Report FPR for non-native writers separately
- Never claim SOTA without reproducible eval

## Hardware
- CPU: statistical detectors <100ms for 500 words
- GPU: transformer ~200-500ms, perturbation ~2-5s

# Methodology - Sudarshan AI Detector

## Hybrid Detection Engine

### 1. Perplexity Analysis
- Uses distilgpt2 / gpt2 as surrogate scorer.
- Computes mean negative log-likelihood.
- AI text typically has lower perplexity under GPT-2 family.
- Mapping: log_ppl -> sigmoid to AI likelihood.
- Limitation: surrogate; true perplexity needs generator's own model (unavailable for closed models).

### 2. Burstiness Analysis
- Sentence length coefficient of variation (CV).
- TTR variance across sentences.
- Human: high burstiness (CV 0.5-1.0, varied lengths).
- AI: uniform (CV 0.2-0.5).
- AI likelihood = 1 - normalized burstiness.

### 3. Stylometric Analysis
- TTR, bigram repetition, function word ratio, paragraph CV.
- AI indicators: low repetition, very regular paragraph lengths, very high TTR +

## Recommended
- **HC3**: Human vs ChatGPT comparison, English + Chinese. https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hello-SimpleAI/HC3
- **M4**: Multi-generator, multi-domain, multilingual. https://huggingface.co/datasets/GenAI-M4/M4
- **RAID**: Robust AI Detection dataset, 11 generators, paraphrase attacks. https://huggingface.co/datasets/liamdugan/raid
- **TuringBench**: 20 generators, Turing test. https://github.com/jonathanpeyre/turingbench

## Hindi / Hinglish
- Custom collection required:
  - Human: Hindi Wikipedia, news (BBC Hindi, Dainik Jagran), Hindi stories, government docs
  - Hinglish: Twitter, YouTube comments, WhatsApp-style (anonymized), Bollywood forums
  - AI: Generate via ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama with prompts in Hindi/Hinglish
  - Include human-edited AI and AI-e

# Limitations & Ethics

1. **No Proof**: Detector scores are statistical signals, not proof of authorship. Never claim certainty.
2. **Short Text**: <50 words inherently inconclusive. <10 words rejected.
3. **Non-native & Hinglish**: May have higher false positives due to simpler syntax. We prioritize low FPR and use IndicBERT.
4. **Paraphrased / Edited AI**: Paraphrasing and human editing significantly reduce detection. Mixed-authorship module attempts but not perfect.
5. **Unseen Generators**: Performance drops on unseen LLMs. Generator-held-out testing required.
6. **Perplexity Surrogate**: Using GPT-2 to score text from Claude/Gemini is surrogate, not true perplexity.
7. **Watermark**: Only works if text was watermarked with known compatible scheme and key.

# Benchmarks

## Metrics
- AUROC
- AUPRC
- Precision, Recall
- FPR, FNR (focus on low FPR)
- Calibration Error (ECE)
- Inference latency

## Expected Baselines (to be measured, not fabricated)
- Statistical detectors alone: AUROC ~0.70-0.80 on in-domain
- + Fine-tuned XLM-R: AUROC ~0.85-0.92 on in-domain, ~0.75-0.85 generator-held-out
- Low FPR target: FPR <5% at 80% recall for English, <10% for Hinglish

## Reporting
- Always report per language, per generator, per domain
- Report FPR for non-native writers separately
- Never claim SOTA without reproducible eval

- CPU: statistical detectors <100ms for 500 words

# Methodology - Sudarshan AI Detector

## Hybrid Detection Engine

### 1. Perplexity Analysis
- Uses distilgpt2 / gpt2 as surrogate scorer.
- Computes mean negative log-likelihood.
- AI text typically has lower perplexity under GPT-2 family.
- Mapping: log_ppl -> sigmoid to AI likelihood.
- Limitation: surrogate; true perplexity needs generator's own model (unavailable for closed models).

### 2. Burstiness Analysis
- Sentence length coefficient of variation (CV).
- TTR variance across sentences.
- Human: high burstiness (CV 0.5-1.0, varied lengths).
- AI: uniform (CV 0.2-0.5).
- AI likelihood = 1 - normalized burstiness.

### 3. Stylometric Analysis
- TTR, bigram repetition, function word ratio, paragraph CV.
- AI indicators: low repetition, very regular paragraph lengths, very high TTR +

1. **No Proof**: Detector scores are statistical signals, not proof of authorship. Never claim certainty.
2. **Short Text**: <50 words inherently inconclusive. <10 words rejected.
3. **Non-native & Hinglish**: May have higher false positives due to simpler syntax. We prioritize low FPR and use IndicBERT.

## Hybrid Detection Engine

### 1. Perplexity Analysis
- Uses distilgpt2 / gpt2 as surrogate scorer.
- Computes mean negative log-likelihood.
- AI text typically has lower perplexity under GPT-2 family.
- Mapping: log_ppl -> sigmoid to AI likelihood.
- Limitation: surrogate; true perplexity needs generator's own model (unavailable for closed models).

### 2. Burstiness Analysis
- Sentence length coefficient of variation (CV).
- TTR variance across sentences.
- Human: high burstiness (CV 0.5-1.0, varied lengths).
- AI: uniform (CV 0.2-0.5).
- AI likelihood = 1 - normalized burstiness.

### 3. Stylometric Analysis
- TTR, bigram repetition, function word ratio, paragraph CV.
- AI indicators: low repetition, very regular paragraph lengths, very high TTR +

# Benchmarks

## Metrics
- AUROC
- AUPRC
- Precision, Recall
- FPR, FNR (focus on low FPR)
- Calibration Error (ECE)
- Inference latency

## Expected Baselines (to be measured, not fabricated)
- Statistical detectors alone: AUROC ~0.70-0.80 on in-domain
- + Fine-tuned XLM-R: AUROC ~0.85-0.92 on in-domain, ~0.75-0.85 generator-held-out
- Low FPR target: FPR <5% at 80% recall for English, <10% for Hinglish

## Reporting
- Always report per language, per generator, per domain
- Report FPR for non-native writers separately
- Never claim SOTA without reproducible eval

## Hardware
- CPU: statistical detectors <100ms for 500 words
- GPU: transformer ~200-500ms, perturbation ~2-5s

# Benchmarks

## Metrics
- AUROC
- AUPRC
- Precision, Recall
- FPR, FNR (focus on low FPR)
- Calibration Error (ECE)
- Inference latency

## Expected Baselines (to be measured, not fabricated)
- Statistical detectors alone: AUROC ~0.70-0.80 on in-domain
- + Fine-tuned XLM-R: AUROC ~0.85-0.92 on in-domain, ~0.75-0.85 generator-held-out
- Low FPR target: FPR <5% at 80% recall for English, <10% for Hinglish

## Reporting
- Always report per language, per generator, per domain
- Report FPR for non-native writers separately
- Never claim SOTA without reproducible eval

## Hardware
- CPU: statistical detectors <100ms for 500 words
- GPU: transformer ~200-500ms, perturbation ~2-5s

# Calibration

## Goals
- Produce calibrated AI-likelihood in [0,1]
- Low false-positive rate, especially for Hindi/Hinglish and non-native English
- Reliability: predicted probability matches empirical frequency

## Methods
- **Isotonic Regression**: non-parametric calibration on held-out validation
- **Platt Scaling**: logistic regression on scores (for transformer)
- **Temperature Scaling**: for overconfident models

## Procedure
1. Collect held-out set with balanced human/AI, multiple generators, multiple languages
2. Get raw scores from each detector
3. Fit isotonic regressor per detector on human=0, AI=1
4. For fusion, fit second-level calibrator on weighted ensemble

## Thresholds
- AI_THRESHOLD=0.65 (high precision)
- HUMAN_THRESHOLD=0.35
- Inconclusive zone 0.35-0.65 or low confid

# Calibration

## Goals
- Produce calibrated AI-likelihood in [0,1]
- Low false-positive rate, especially for Hindi/Hinglish and non-native English
- Reliability: predicted probability matches empirical frequency

## Methods
- **Isotonic Regression**: non-parametric calibration on held-out validation
- **Platt Scaling**: logistic regression on scores (for transformer)
- **Temperature Scaling**: for overconfident models

## Procedure
1. Collect held-out set with balanced human/AI, multiple generators, multiple languages
2. Get raw scores from each detector
3. Fit isotonic regressor per detector on human=0, AI=1
4. For fusion, fit second-level calibrator on weighted ensemble

## Thresholds
- AI_THRESHOLD=0.65 (high precision)
- HUMAN_THRESHOLD=0.35
- Inconclusive zone 0.35-0.65 or low confid

# Calibration

## Goals
- Produce calibrated AI-likelihood in [0,1]
- Low false-positive rate, especially for Hindi/Hinglish and non-native English
- Reliability: predicted probability matches empirical frequency

## Methods
- **Isotonic Regression**: non-parametric calibration on held-out validation
- **Platt Scaling**: logistic regression on scores (for transformer)
- **Temperature Scaling**: for overconfident models

## Procedure
1. Collect held-out set with balanced human/AI, multiple generators, multiple languages
2. Get raw scores from each detector
3. Fit isotonic regressor per detector on human=0, AI=1
4. For fusion, fit second-level calibrator on weighted ensemble

# Datasets

## Recommended
- **HC3**: Human vs ChatGPT comparison, English + Chinese. https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hello-SimpleAI/HC3
- **M4**: Multi-generator, multi-domain, multilingual. https://huggingface.co/datasets/GenAI-M4/M4
- **RAID**: Robust AI Detection dataset, 11 generators, paraphrase attacks. https://huggingface.co/datasets/liamdugan/raid
- **TuringBench**: 20 generators, Turing test. https://github.com/jonathanpeyre/turingbench

## Hindi / Hinglish
- Custom collection required:
  - Human: Hindi Wikipedia, news (BBC Hindi, Dainik Jagran), Hindi stories, government docs
  - Hinglish: Twitter, YouTube comments, WhatsApp-style (anonymized), Bollywood forums
  - AI: Generate via ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama with prompts in Hindi/Hinglish
  - Include human-edited AI and AI-e
